originalTitle: Microsoft reveals strong cloud growth amid financial reporting overhaul

content: Microsoft just posted the first quarter of its 2027 fiscal financial results. The software maker made $92.3 billion in revenue and a net income of $33.6 billion during Q1. Revenue is up 19 percent, and net income has increased by 32 percent. It’s a new financial year for Microsoft, so the company is changing up how it reports its finances by splitting its businesses into two segments for the first time. Gone are the previous segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. It’s now just Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer. Agents and Infra, which includes businesses like Azure, Microsoft 365 commercial and consumer, and server products, makes up 83 percent ($76.8 billion) of the overall $92.3 billion of Microsoft’s revenue and has increased 25 percent year-over-year. The big changes to Microsoft’s financial reporting also mean we will now see the company disclose Azure revenue on a quarterly basis. Azure contributed $33.17 billion in revenue this quarter, up 48 percent year-over-year. Devices and Consumer, which includes Windows, Xbox, Surface, and Microsoft’s search and advertising businesses, makes up the remaining 17 percent ($15.5 billion) of Microsoft’s $92.3 billion in revenues this quarter — a decrease of three percent. [Image: Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra arrived on shelves earlier this month. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/VERGE_10_04_2026_0184.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Windows OEM and devices revenue is down 22 percent year-over-year, amid a RAMageddon crisis that has seen the overall PC market dropped by 20 percent in the recent quarter. Microsoft blames the revenue drop on the benefit of Windows 10 end of support during the prior year, as well as OEM inventory drawdowns and a weaker PC market. Microsoft launched Intel- and Qualcomm-powered Surface Pro 12 and Surface Laptop 8 devices just before its new financial year began, and the company even refreshed its smaller Surface Pro and Surface Laptop with Qualcomm’s X2 Plus chips during the quarter. Surface prices are higher than ever thanks to RAMageddon, and the PC market looks like it’s going to go through a very tough time during Microsoft’s 2027 financial year and beyond. Microsoft CFO Amy Hood said on the company’s earnings call that she expects Windows OEM revenue to decline again next quarter, around “the mid 30s,” and a decline is expected to continue throughout the 2027 financial year. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella also remarked on the company’s new hybrid AI push for Windows during the earnings call. “We are executing on our vision to bring hybrid intelligence to every desk in every home, making every PC a secure agent box,” said Nadella. “As more capable models run locally, we see an opportunity to make more intelligence effectively unmetered.” Microsoft and Nvidia unveiled a range of RTX Spark laptops earlier this month, including the Surface Laptop Ultra. The laptops ship with up to 128GB of unified memory, and are capable of running recent frontier models locally. [Image: The Xbox Series X25 console will mark 25 years of Xbox next month. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/06/XBOX-Series-X25-Limited-Edition_2-1bfdd2858ad74a2180ff-1900x1080-1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Over on the Xbox side, hardware revenue has declined once again year-over-year. Xbox hardware revenue is down 14 percent. Xbox content and services, which includes Game Pass, is down 2 percent, too. Microsoft is still not giving an update on Game Pass subscriber numbers, after the company last reported it had 34 million subscribers more than two years ago. Overall Xbox revenue is down 2 percent. The first quarter of the 2027 financial year for Xbox has been dominated by a “reset” with thousands of layoffs and studios spun off. The layoffs aren’t over yet, with rumors more could arrive in November and January. In a memo earlier this year, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said “we will return Xbox to player and revenue growth” by the end of fiscal year 2027 (which runs through next June). The aim, as Sharma puts it, is to “scale what works” so that by fiscal year 2030 Xbox is “halfway to our long-term daily-player goal with sustained double-digit growth in players and engagement and industry leading margins.” Sharma posted on X that Xbox was “making progress, with a lot more work ahead.” Sharma also revealed that PC platform revenue has grown in double digits this quarter, and that “console sales remain constrained by supply, with more demand than consoles available.” [Media: https://twitter.com/asha_shar/status/2115574497621463499] Hood says Xbox hardware revenue will decline again next quarter, but Xbox content and services revenue is expected to increase in the “mid to high single digits.” Sharma says Microsoft is “working to get more consoles into players’ hands, including through our expanded refurbishment program.” Microsoft’s cloud revenues were really the star of the earnings show again this quarter, a phrase I seem to always write every few months. Microsoft Cloud revenue contributed $63.9 billion towards Microsoft’s revenues this quarter, almost 70 percent. That’s up 30 percent year-over-year, thanks to strong demand for Azure and Microsoft 365 commercial cloud. Microsoft 365 commercial cloud revenue itself also grew 18 percent, thanks to higher revenue per user and upselling of premium options like Microsoft 365 Copilot, E5, and E7. Microsoft 365 consumer cloud revenue has also grown by 17 percent, driven by growth in revenue per user and subscriber growth of 7 percent. chineseTitle: 微软在财务报告改革中透露出强劲的云增长
chineseSummary: 微软刚刚发布了2027年第一季度财报。这家软件制造商第一季度的收入为 923 亿美元，净利润为 336 亿美元。收入增长 19%，净利润增长 32%。这是微软的新财政年度，因此该公司正在改变 [...]
chineseContent: 微软刚刚发布了2027年第一季度财报。这家软件制造商第一季度的收入为 923 亿美元，净利润为 336 亿美元。收入增长 19%，净利润增长 32%。对于微软来说，这是一个新的财政年度，因此该公司正在改变其财务报告方式，首次将其业务分为两个部分。以前的部分已经不复存在：生产力和业务流程、智能云和更多个人计算。现在只有代理和基础设施、设备和消费者。代理和基础设施包括 Azure、Microsoft 365 商业和消费者以及服务器产品等业务，占微软 923 亿美元总收入的 83%（768 亿美元），并且同比增长 25%。微软财务报告的重大变化也意味着我们现在将看到该公司按季度披露 Azure 收入。 Azure 本季度贡献了 331.7 亿美元的收入，同比增长 48%。设备和消费者业务，包括 Windows、Xbox、Surface 以及微软的搜索和广告业务，占微软本季度 923 亿美元收入的剩余 17%（155 亿美元）——下降了 3%。 [图片：微软 Surface Laptop Ultra 于本月初上架。 https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/10/VERGE_10_04_2026_0184.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] 由于 RAMgeddon 危机，整个 PC 市场在最近一个季度下降了 20%，Windows OEM 和设备收入同比下降 22%。微软将收入下降归咎于上一年 Windows 10 支持终止以及 OEM 库存减少
